title: Bound dense cross-port thin-query capacity at 528 requests (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration; no new kappa or selected-frontier change.

Assuming fifteen missing scalar observation dimensions per independent port, dense cross-port linear queries, adaptive feedback and arbitrary deterministic decoding still need total output capacity at least `15P`.

```text
528 requests, 104 ports: total capacity >= 1560
  capacity <= 3 requires at least 504 capacity-three requests
528 requests, 112 ports: total capacity >= 1680
  capacity <= 4 requires at least 96 capacity-four requests
```

If requests stay scalar, the alternative requires at least 1032 or 1152 newly supplied free dimensions. The proof gives the exact abstract minimum with added side information. A request's capacity counts its scalar output coordinates, independently of its support across ports or its native frame rank.

This extends the multi-port question in Matarener's [PR #5996](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5996), head `47242572d3b22ce49371245edc561dd75bf263e8`. Its reported per-port quotient dimension is an explicit cited premise, not replayed or validated here. The general rank principle is classical and already appears in the repository's outside-input probe and centre-information work. The new result is this conditional thin-pool contract and capacity distribution. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19227495).

## Evidence

Before, the cited thin-pool exclusion restricts requests to a port. The new proof permits cross-port scalar rows and data-dependent request selection, and gives necessary vector-output budgets.

Local warning-strict normal and optimized runs pass `PASS_CROSS_PORT_THIN_CAPACITY`: 304,993 binary subspace triples, 4,230 independent literal fiber comparisons, 116 rational recoding/side-information fixtures, 510 complete adaptive transcripts, 255 ambiguous shortened transcripts, four semantic controls and four invalid-input rejections. Completeness is also checked against every square binary matrix through dimension four. Registered commands took 0.24 and 0.23 seconds locally, only a replay-budget observation.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/cross-port-thin-capacity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/cross-port-thin-capacity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/cross-port-thin-capacity
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/cross-port-thin-capacity --check-source-history
```

Metadata, both registered commands, committed bytes/source history, the official six-file export, export integrity and a read-only Git-free optimized replay pass. CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64; standard library only. Other machines may substitute their CPython 3.12 path. The standalone verifier needs no Git, network or predecessor source. Optional `--receipt PATH` creates a hash-bound receipt outside the package.

## Limitations

The universal statement rests on the written proof. The thin-pool application assumes the cited quotient deficit and independent port inputs, with exactly the declared free information. Binding actual multi-port semantics and every free operation to this contract is unproved. Full vector responses can carry many coordinates and are not excluded. Native frame rank is not identified with output capacity. Physical realization, chronological availability, dirty restoration, full paid invoice, compiler, stock, precision and tape costs remain open. No complete multiplication theorem, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. No predecessor scientific replay, Lean or selected cold replay was run.

## Related open work

- #5996 supplies the reported per-port deficit and asks about multi-port channels; this adds a conditional dense-query capacity bound without rechecking its computation.
- #5994 excludes helper-split cuts on the PR5907 word; it studies target splitting rather than the thin-query observation capacity here.
- #5975 compresses ordinary events on PR5907 while preserving its invoice; this supplies no event rewrite or new word.
- #5960 reviews the PR5827/5907 construction and funding; this performs no such review.
- #5270 changes the p19 controller and prices its uncoded endpoint; the present theorem assumes the reported fifteen-deficit independent-port contract and does not transfer to that changed word.
- #5440 prices a coded p19 chain with separate precompilation obligations; no claim about that chain's observation capacity is made here.
- #5298 studies joint bit/complex whole-job accounting; its mass premise differs from independent scalar-observation capacity.

## Open next questions

1. Can one physical query meet the necessary multi-output capacity distribution at favorable complete cost? First specify its maps and native tariff, then restoration and chronological availability.
2. Does the actual multi-port caller satisfy the direct-sum observation hypotheses? Supply input-coordinate and free-span maps before applying the numerical bound physically.
3. Can a changed producer cheaply supply the required extra free dimensions? Price one independently new observable and its complete consumer/restoration bill.
